query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_theme
per_column.rationale: Extracted categorical variable with well-separated, interpretable themes (billing, auth, ui, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against resolution time. Genuinely opens a new relationship axis absent from the original table.

per_column.name: theme_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: A precomputed group aggregate of the focus itself keyed by theme. It restates the focus rather than providing an external associational variable; grouping on it is equivalent to grouping on issue_theme, adding no independent relationship.

per_column.name: channel_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Group mean of the focus by channel, which is already an original column. It is a derivative of the focus, not an external predictor, so it collapses exploration into a lookup of channel.

per_column.name: priority_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Group mean of the focus by priority (already present). Restates the focus keyed by an existing segmentation; not an independent associational variable.

per_column.name: resolution_vs_theme_avg
per_column.rationale: A residual of the focus minus its theme mean. This is a transform of the focus variable itself, with fine-grained near-unique values that support no clean segmentation; it is opaque restatement, not an external comparison axis.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: A numeric re-encoding of the existing priority column. Adds no new information beyond priority; it is a restatement of an existing segmentation dimension.

judge.rationale: Only issue_theme is a genuine new, interpretable segmentation variable that opens an informative relationship with resolution time. The remaining five columns are either precomputed group aggregates of the focus (theme/channel/priority averages), a residual transform of the focus, or a mere re-encoding of an existing column. These restate the focus or existing dimensions rather than introducing external associational variables, and one (resolution_vs_theme_avg) is too fine-grained to segment on. As a set they weakly support interpretable relationship discovery.
